construction_markdown:
Let
\[
p(T)=T^{16}+T^5+T^3+T^2+1,\qquad F=\mathbb F_2[T]/(p),
\]
and let \(\theta=T\bmod p\). Define the deterministic evaluation set
\[
V=\left\{\sum_{i=0}^{14}u_i\theta^i:u_i\in\mathbb F_2\right\},
\qquad |V|=2^{15},
\]
ordered by the binary integer \(\sum_i u_i2^i\).

The outer code is the shortened Reed–Solomon code
\[
A=\{(P(v))_{v\in V}:P\in F[Z],\ \deg P\le64\}.
\]
For \(a=\sum_{i=0}^{15}a_i\theta^i\in F\), define
\[
\phi(a)=\left(a_0+\sum_{i=1}^{15}a_ix_i\right)_{x\in\mathbb F_2^{15}},
\]
with \(x\) in binary-integer order. This is an explicit \(\mathbb F_2\)-linear isomorphism from \(F\) onto \(\operatorname{RM}(1,15)\).

Apply the shared affine-inner concatenation lemma from `algebraic-03`:
\[
C=\{(\phi(P(v)))_{v\in V}:\deg P\le64\}.
\]
There is no padding, puncturing, shortening, or random choice in the final binary construction.

discussion_posts.body_markdown:
Let \(Q=2^m\). If an \(\mathbb F_Q\)-linear outer code of length \(N\) and dimension \(K\) is concatenated through coordinate-dependent \(\mathbb F_2\)-isomorphisms onto \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)\), then some nonzero concatenated word has weight at most
\[
(N-K+1)\frac{Q2^{m-2}}{Q-1}.
\]
Indeed, Singleton supplies an outer word supported on at most \(N-K+1\) coordinates, and averaging its nonzero scalar multiples uses the exact average weight \(Q2^{m-2}/(Q-1)\) of the nonzero Reed–Muller words.

discussion_posts.body_markdown:
For \(Q=65536\), \(N=32768\), and \(K=66\), the scalar-orbit bound is
\[
32703\cdot16384\cdot\frac{65536}{65535}=535814127.874\ldots<535822336.
\]
Thus no \(\mathbb F_{2^{16}}\)-linear outer code of dimension 66 can beat the submitted \(K=65\) construction through RM(1,15) symbol descent, even with coordinate-dependent inner isomorphisms.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Does there exist an \(\mathbb F_2\)-additive, non-\(\mathbb F_{2^{16}}\)-linear subspace of \(F^{32768}\) of binary dimension at least 1041 whose RM(1,15)-descended words all have weight at least 535822336? Such a space evades scalar-orbit averaging; degree-65 restricted-coefficient attempts need a uniform condition forcing every 65-root word to hit the unique all-one inner symbol.

proof_markdown:
# Reed–Solomon code with affine binary descent

## Theorem

There is a deterministic binary linear code with exact parameters
\[
[2^{30},1040,535{,}822{,}336]_2.
\]
Its exact rate is \(1040/2^{30}=65/2^{26}\).

## Explicit field

Put
\[
p(T)=T^{16}+T^5+T^3+T^2+1.
\]
Repeated squaring modulo \(p\) gives
\[
T^{2^8}\equiv T^8+T^7+T^3+T,
\qquad T^{2^{16}}\equiv T.
\]
Let \(h=T^8+T^7+T^3\), and set
\[
A=T^6+T^5+T^4+T^3+T^2+1,
\]
\[
B=T^{14}+T^{12}+T^{10}+T^8+T^5+T^4+T^3.
\]
Direct multiplication over \(\mathbb F_2[T]\) gives \(Ap+Bh=1\). Hence
\(\gcd(p,T^{2^8}+T)=1\), while \(p\mid T^{2^{16}}+T\). Every proper divisor of 16 divides 8, so the standard Frobenius factorization criterion proves that \(p\) is irreducible. Thus
\[
F=\mathbb F_2[T]/(p)
\]
is the specified field of order \(2^{16}\), with basis \(1,\theta,\ldots,\theta^{15}\).

## Outer and inner codes

Let
\[
V=\left\{\sum_{i=0}^{14}u_i\theta^i:u_i\in\mathbb F_2\right\}.
\]
The basis property gives \(|V|=2^{15}\). Evaluate every polynomial \(P\in F[Z]\) of degree at most 64 on the points of \(V\). Evaluation is injective because a nonzero polynomial of degree at most 64 cannot vanish at all 32768 points. The outer code therefore has dimension 65 over \(F\), and every nonzero outer word has at least
\[
32768-64=32704
\]
nonzero symbols.

For \(a=\sum_{i=0}^{15}a_i\theta^i\), define
\[
\phi(a)=\left(a_0+\sum_{i=1}^{15}a_ix_i\right)_{x\in\mathbb F_2^{15}}.
\]
This is an injective binary-linear map onto \(\operatorname{RM}(1,15)\). If some \(a_i\), \(i\ge1\), is nonzero, the corresponding affine function is balanced and has weight \(2^{14}\). If all those coefficients vanish, the only nonzero possibility is \(a=1\), whose image has weight \(2^{15}\). Hence every nonzero inner word has weight at least \(2^{14}\).

## Binary linearity, length, and dimension

Define
\[
C=\{(\phi(P(v)))_{v\in V}:P\in F[Z],\deg P\le64\}.
\]
Both evaluation and \(\phi\) are \(\mathbb F_2\)-linear. Their composite is injective, so
\[
\dim_{\mathbb F_2}C=16\cdot65=1040.
\]
There are \(2^{15}\) blocks of length \(2^{15}\), giving
\[
n=2^{15}2^{15}=2^{30}=1{,}073{,}741{,}824.
\]

## Minimum distance

For nonzero \(P\), at least 32704 blocks are nonzero, and each contributes at least \(2^{14}\) ones. Therefore
\[
\operatorname{wt}(C(P))\ge32704\cdot2^{14}
=(2^{15}-2^6)2^{14}
=2^{29}-2^{20}
=535{,}822{,}336.
\]

The bound is attained. Fix 64 points \(R\subset V\) and let
\[
g(Z)=\prod_{r\in R}(Z-r).
\]
The set \(g(V\setminus R)\) has at most 32704 elements, fewer than \(|F^*|=65535\). Choose \(z\in F^*\setminus g(V\setminus R)\), for example the first such element in polynomial-basis order, and put \(P=z^{-1}g\). Then \(P\) has exactly the 64 roots in \(R\), and \(P(v)\ne1\) elsewhere. Every remaining symbol lies in \(F\setminus\{0,1\}\), so all 32704 nonzero blocks have weight exactly \(2^{14}\). Thus the displayed lower bound is the exact minimum distance.

## Optimality inside the field-linear descent architecture

More generally, suppose an \(F\)-linear outer code of length 32768 and dimension \(K\) is concatenated through arbitrary coordinate-dependent binary-linear isomorphisms onto \(\operatorname{RM}(1,15)\). Singleton supplies a nonzero outer word supported on at most \(32768-K+1\) positions. As a nonzero scalar \(\lambda\in F^*\) varies, each supported inner block ranges once over all 65535 nonzero RM(1,15) words. Their average weight is
\[
\frac{32768+65534\cdot16384}{65535}
=16384\frac{65536}{65535}.
\]
If \(K\ge66\), some scalar multiple consequently has weight at most
\[
32703\cdot16384\frac{65536}{65535}
=535814127.874\ldots<535822336.
\]
It violates the target. Hence \(K\le65\), and the submitted \(k=1040\) construction is optimal within this entire field-linear outer/RM-inner architecture.
